core.title: Take a component's side, layer, type, file-name suffix and weight from one canonical catalog entry
core.given: A plan artifact or doc derives components, names file-name patterns or estimates effort, or the catalog is edited. The canonical component type catalog (provided by the structure profile) lists every component type by side and layer, with per-language file-name suffix, description and complexity weight, derived from the implementation-side conventions.
core.when: You set a component's side, layer, type, the side/layer values of its URN, its file-name pattern or its weight.
core.then: Take all of a component's values from one matching catalog entry: side, layer, type, the suffix that entry defines for the component's target language, and the weight.
prefer: Take the side/layer values of a component URN from the catalog's structure; look entries up by the catalog's side.layer.type key.
Pick the type whose catalog description fits; estimate effort with the catalog weights.
Catalog edits: keep each type complete (per-language suffix, description, weight) and derived from the implementation-side conventions; flag mismatches, never pick ad hoc.
avoid: Ad-hoc types, layers, sides or weights; tweaking weights to shape an estimate.
Mixing values across entries or languages.
core.why: One canonical catalog keeps component derivation and effort estimates consistent with the implementation-side conventions instead of ad hoc.
evidence: Every planned component's side, layer and type resolve to exactly one entry in the canonical component type catalog.
Each declared file-name pattern equals that same entry's suffix for the component's target language (an entry with no suffix for a language means the type is unavailable there).
Each weight used in effort/footprint estimation equals that same entry's weight.
verification: Resolve each planned component by the tuple (side, layer, type, target language) against the profile's component type catalog; the suffix and weight must come from that single tuple, not merely exist somewhere in the catalog.
Resolve entries by side and layer, never by suffix alone; suffixes can collide across entries, and an entry may list several alternative suffixes for a language — any listed alternative is valid.
A catalog entry with no suffix for a language means the type is unavailable in that language.
The stack's check validates the catalog itself (each type complete and in sync with the implementation-side conventions); checking plan entries against the catalog is reviewer-judged.
No aggregation formula is prescribed for weights: do not flag an estimate for how weights are combined, only for weights that differ from the matching entry.

values: component side/layer/type/URN, file pattern or weight added or changed in a plan artifact
component values not from one matching catalog entry
catalog type missing suffix/description/weight or out of sync with the implementation conventions

fires: Planner derives the components a feature needs and assigns side, layer and type.
Planner writes a component URN (its side/layer values) into a plan artifact or doc.
Planner states the expected file-name pattern for a planned component in a given language.
Planner estimates effort/footprint using component complexity weights.
The component type catalog itself is added to, edited or validated.
doesNotFire: Implementer coding an already-planned component (the implementation-side conventions govern).
Planning text that names no components, types, file patterns or weights (e.g. pure acceptance wording).
Docs unrelated to component derivation, file patterns, effort estimation or the catalog.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's canonical component type catalog: every component type keyed by side and layer, each with per-language file-name suffix(es), description and complexity weight; side.layer.type is the lookup key and supplies the side/layer values of component URNs; an entry with no suffix for a language makes the type unavailable there; the catalog is derived from the implementation-side conventions.
profileRequirements.bunValue: sharedNodes[context.component-type-catalog] in bun.json: sides backend|frontend; layers presentation, application, domain, integration; backend languages python|typescript, frontend languages dart|typescript; every entry 'type — suffix(es) per language — description — weight'; lookup key side.layer.type (full entry list in that node)

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds whose component derivations, file-name patterns and weights this rule covers.

neutralityNotes: The catalog's contents are stack data: the sides (backend|frontend), the layer names, the per-language suffix sets (python/typescript/dart), the weights and the type inventory all belong to the realization. The core carries only the obligation to take every component value from one matching entry; the catalog reaches it through the proposed profile key roles.layer_catalog#component_type_catalog, and the full entry list stays in bun.json's shared node context.component-type-catalog (summarized, not duplicated, in profileRequirements.bunValue). The concrete example entries, the suffix-collision/multi-suffix/language-missing enumerations, the validator id, the shared-node id and the wagon/WMBT note terms have no stack-neutral equivalent and are bunOnly. The language dimension itself ('the component's target language') is kept because the catalog is keyed per language; which languages exist is profile data carried by the catalog. The side/layer role vocabulary (presentation, application, domain, integration) appears only inside the catalog data, not as a named structure in the core.
